MediBook Online Appointment
Booking System

A production-deployed, full-stack healthcare appointment platform built on Spring Boot microservices and React. Patients find doctors, book slots, pay online with Razorpay, and access electronic medical records — all from one unified platform.

Overview

Project Synopsis

MediBook is a full-stack Online Appointment Booking System that enables patients to search for healthcare providers (doctors, consultants, therapists, specialists), view available time slots, and book appointments — all from a single unified platform. Built with Spring Boot microservices backend and React frontend, fully deployed on AWS EC2 with Docker Compose.

11
Microservices
3
User Roles
50+
API Endpoints
8
MySQL Databases
AWS
EC2 Deployed
👤
Patient Portal
Browse doctors by specialization, view real-time slot availability, book & cancel appointments, make online payments (Razorpay UPI/Card/Wallet), access electronic medical records and prescriptions, submit star ratings & reviews.
🩺
Provider Dashboard
Configure weekly availability slots (individual or recurring), view today's appointment schedule, mark consultations complete, create electronic medical records with diagnosis & prescriptions, track earnings and revenue analytics.
🛡️
Admin Control Panel
Verify provider credentials, manage all platform users (deactivate/reactivate), monitor all appointments platform-wide, view payment transactions, trigger refunds, broadcast platform-wide notifications to any user group.
🔔
Smart Notifications
Real-time in-app + email notifications powered by RabbitMQ. Booking confirmation, 24h & 1h pre-appointment reminders, cancellation alerts, payment receipts, follow-up date reminders auto-triggered from medical records.
💳
Razorpay Payments
Full Razorpay integration — order creation, HMAC signature verification, Card/UPI/Wallet modes. Automatic refund processing on cancellation. Revenue analytics dashboard for admin and per-provider earnings breakdown.
🔐
JWT + OTP + OAuth2
Two-factor authentication with OTP sent via SMTP email. Google OAuth2 social login. JWT-based stateless auth across all services validated at API Gateway. Role-based access control: Patient, Provider, Admin.

System Architecture Diagram

All client requests flow through Nginx → Spring Cloud API Gateway (port 8080) which validates JWT and routes to microservices discovered via Eureka.

Diagrams

Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD)

Core entities and relationships. Each service database is isolated — cross-service references are application-level only.

Diagrams

Class Diagrams — All Services

Each microservice follows the same 5-layer pattern: Entity → Repository Interface → Service Interface → ServiceImpl → REST Resource (Controller). This enforces loose coupling and separation of concerns.

🏗️
Architecture Pattern: Entity (JPA POJO) → Repository (Spring Data) → Service Interface (contract) → ServiceImpl (business logic) → REST Resource (HTTP exposure). Zero business logic in controllers.
🔐 Auth / User Service
com.medibook.auth · Port 8081
auth_db
Security gateway. Handles registration with BCrypt password hashing, OTP-based two-factor login, JWT generation/validation, Google OAuth2 social login, profile management, forgot password flow with email OTP, admin registration with secret code.
User EntityUserRepository AuthServiceImplAuthResource JwtUtilOTP Cache OAuth2JavaMailSender
🛡️ Admin Service
com.medibook.admin · Port 8089
auth_db (shared read)
Admin-exclusive platform management. Calls auth-service via Feign client for user data. Handles user deactivation/reactivation, provider verification/disabling, adding new admin accounts at runtime, role-based user filtering.
AdminResourceAdminServiceImpl UserClient (Feign)Admin-only JWT UserResponse DTO
🩺 Provider Service
com.medibook.provider · Port 8082
provider_db
Healthcare professional profiles. Stores specialization, qualification, experience, clinic details. Feign client calls auth-service GET /auth/profile/{userId} to enrich responses with fullName/email/phone. Admin verification gate before appearing in searches.
Provider EntityProviderRepository ProviderServiceImplProviderResource UserClient (Feign)ProviderDetailResponse
📅 Schedule Service
com.medibook.schedule · Port 8083
schedule_db
Availability slot management. Add individual or bulk slots, generate recurring slots (DAILY/WEEKLY patterns), block/unblock slots. Enforces state machine: Available → Booked → Released. SlotExpiryScheduler runs every 30 min to purge past slots.
AvailabilitySlot EntitySlotRepository ScheduleServiceImplScheduleResource SlotExpirySchedulerSlotRequest DTO
🗓️ Appointment Service
com.medibook.appointment · Port 8084
appointment_db
Core booking orchestrator. bookAppointment() calls Schedule-Service (Feign) to mark slot as BOOKED. On completion publishes BOOKING_CONFIRMED event to RabbitMQ. NoShowDetectionScheduler runs hourly. cancelAppointment() releases slot and triggers refund.
Appointment EntityAppointmentRepository AppointmentServiceImplSlotClient (Feign) AppointmentEventPublisherNoShowScheduler
💳 Payment Service
com.medibook.payment · Port 8085
payment_db
Full Razorpay integration. initiatePayment() creates Razorpay order. verifyPayment() validates HMAC SHA256 signature. initiateRefund() calls Razorpay refund API. getTotalRevenue() aggregates all SUCCESS payments. Provider earnings view via getPaymentsByProvider().
Payment EntityPaymentRepository PaymentServiceImplPaymentResource Razorpay SDKPaymentRequest/Response DTO
⭐ Review Service
com.medibook.review · Port 8086
review_db
Post-consultation ratings. One review per appointment (UNIQUE constraint on appointment_id). Ratings 1–5 stars. Supports anonymous reviews. avgRatingByProviderId() query used by Provider-Service to update provider's avgRating field. Admin can delete inappropriate reviews.
Review EntityReviewRepository ReviewServiceImplReviewResource AvgRating QueryisAnonymous flag
🔔 Notification Service
com.medibook.notification · Port 8087
notification_db
RabbitMQ consumer for appointment events. send() persists in-app notification + sends SMTP email. sendBulk() is @Async for platform-wide broadcasts. Tracks read/unread state. getUnreadCount() powers the bell badge. Admin can broadcast to all user groups.
Notification EntityNotificationRepository NotificationServiceImplNotificationResource RabbitMQ ListenerJavaMailSender @Async
📋 Record Service
com.medibook.record · Port 8088
record_db
Electronic health records created by provider after marking appointment COMPLETED. Stores diagnosis, prescription, clinical notes, document attachment URL, follow-up date. Follow-up date triggers automated patient reminder email. Patients read own records; providers read what they created; admins read-only audit.
MedicalRecord EntityRecordRepository RecordServiceImplRecordResource FollowUp SchedulerattachDocument()

All endpoints route through https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org. Include header Authorization: Bearer <token> for protected routes. Token obtained from POST /auth/verify-otp.

{ "providerId": 1, "date": "2026-05-28", "startTime": "10:30", "endTime": "11:00", "durationMinutes": 30 }

POST/appointments/book Book an appointment (core action)
{ "patientId": 5, "providerId": 1, "slotId": 42, "serviceType": "General Consultation", "modeOfConsultation": "In-Person", "appointmentDate": "2026-05-28", "startTime": "10:30", "endTime": "11:00" }

GET /appointments/patient/5 → all appointments GET /appointments/patient/5/upcoming → upcoming only GET /appointments/provider/1 → provider's appointments GET /appointments/provider/1/date?date=2026-05-28 → by date

Database Schemas

Each microservice maintains its own isolated MySQL database. Schema auto-generated by Spring Data JPA (Hibernate DDL). Cross-service references are logical (application-level), not DB foreign keys.

auth_db · users

ColumnTypeConstraints
user_idINTPK AUTO_INCREMENT
full_nameVARCHAR(100)NOT NULL
emailVARCHAR(255)UNIQUE NOT NULL
password_hashVARCHAR(255)BCrypt encrypted
phoneVARCHAR(20)Required for OTP
roleVARCHAR(20)Patient|Provider|Admin
providerVARCHAR(50)google / null
is_activeBOOLEANDEFAULT TRUE
created_atDATETIMEAuto timestamp
profile_pic_urlTEXTOAuth2 picture URL

appointment_db · appointments

ColumnTypeConstraints
appointment_idINTPK AUTO_INCREMENT
patient_idINTLogical FK → users
provider_idINTLogical FK → providers
slot_idINTLogical FK → slots
service_typeVARCHAR(100)NOT NULL
appointment_dateDATENOT NULL
start_timeTIMENOT NULL
end_timeTIMENOT NULL
statusVARCHAR(20)SCHEDULED|COMPLETED|CANCELLED|NO_SHOW
mode_of_consultationVARCHAR(30)In-Person|Video

Deployment

Full Deployment Guide

Complete step-by-step guide to deploy MediBook on AWS EC2 with Docker Compose, Nginx HTTPS, DuckDNS domain, and Vercel frontend.

AWS
Cloud Provider
EC2
t2.medium
30GB
SSD Storage
Docker
13 Containers
SSL
Let's Encrypt
⚠️
Important: Use t2.medium minimum. t2.micro runs out of memory with 11 microservices. Minimum 30 GB storage — Docker images are large.

Security Group — Inbound Rules

PortServiceSource
22SSHMy IP only (security)
80HTTP → 301 HTTPS redirect0.0.0.0/0
443HTTPS (Nginx)0.0.0.0/0
8080API Gateway (direct access)0.0.0.0/0
8761Eureka Dashboard0.0.0.0/0
15672RabbitMQ Management UI0.0.0.0/0

Step 1 — Connect & Install Dependencies

# Connect to EC2 ssh -i your-key.pem ubuntu@your-ec2-public-ip # Update system sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y # Install Java 17 sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk -y java -version # → openjdk 17 # Install Maven sudo apt install maven -y # Install Docker sudo apt install docker.io -y sudo systemctl start docker && sudo systemctl enable docker sudo usermod -aG docker ubuntu newgrp docker # Install Docker Compose Plugin sudo apt install docker-compose-plugin -y docker compose version # Install Git & Node.js 20 sudo apt install git -y curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash - sudo apt install -y nodejs node --version && npm --version

Step 2 — Clone & Configure

cd ~ git clone https://github.com/your-username/MediBook-Microservices.git cd MediBook-Microservices # Create .env file (CRITICAL — fill with your real values) nano .env
# .env contents: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=root DB_USERNAME=root DB_PASSWORD=root JWT_SECRET=yourSecretKeyHereMakeItLong64CharsMinimum MAIL_USERNAME=youremail@gmail.com MAIL_PASSWORD=your-gmail-app-password RAZORPAY_API_KEY=rzp_test_yourkey RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET=yoursecret GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-google-client-id GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-google-secret GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org/login/oauth2/code/google FRONTEND_URL=https://medibook-client-beryl.vercel.app ADMIN_PASSWORD_1=yourAdminPassword1 ADMIN_PASSWORD_2=yourAdminPassword2

Step 3 — Build & Start Containers

# Validate config docker compose config # Build all images (10–25 minutes) docker compose build # Start all 13 containers in background docker compose up -d # Verify running containers docker ps # Expected: mysql, rabbitmq, eureka, gateway, auth, admin, # provider, schedule, appointment, payment, review, notification, record # View logs docker logs medibook-auth docker logs -f medibook-gateway # live streaming logs docker compose logs --tail=50 # last 50 lines all services

Step 4 — Elastic IP (Prevents IP Change)

# AWS Console → EC2 → Elastic IPs # 1. Allocate new Elastic IP # 2. Actions → Associate with your EC2 instance # Your IP is now FIXED — won't change on stop/start

Step 5 — DuckDNS Domain

# 1. Go to https://www.duckdns.org → Login with Google # 2. Create subdomain: medibook-microservices # 3. Enter your EC2 Elastic IP → Click "update ip" # Domain: medibook-microservices.duckdns.org now points to your EC2

Step 6 — Nginx + SSL (HTTPS)

# Install Nginx sudo apt install nginx -y sudo systemctl start nginx && sudo systemctl enable nginx # Install Certbot (free Let's Encrypt SSL) sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx -y sudo certbot --nginx -d medibook-microservices.duckdns.org # Edit Nginx config sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/medibook
# Nginx config file: server { server_name medibook-microservices.duckdns.org; location / { proxy_pass http://localhost:8080; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade'; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; } listen 443 ssl; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/medibook-microservices.duckdns.org/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/medibook-microservices.duckdns.org/privkey.pem; include /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-nginx.conf; ssl_dhparam /etc/letsencrypt/ssl-dhparams.pem; } server { if ($host = medibook-microservices.duckdns.org) { return 301 https://$host$request_uri; } server_name medibook-microservices.duckdns.org; listen 80; return 404; }
# Enable and reload sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/medibook /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ sudo nginx -t # test config (must show: test is successful) sudo systemctl reload nginx

Step 7 — Vercel Frontend Deploy

# Option A: GitHub auto-deploy (recommended) # 1. Push code to GitHub # 2. Go to vercel.com → New Project → Import Git Repo # 3. Set Environment Variable: # VITE_API_BASE_URL = https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org # 4. Deploy → Live at: https://medibook-client-beryl.vercel.app # Option B: CLI deploy npm install -g vercel cd medibook-frontend echo "VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org" > .env vercel --prod

Step 8 — Verify Deployment

# Check all 13 containers running docker ps # Test API Gateway via HTTPS curl https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org/auth/register # Open in browser: # Eureka Dashboard: http://your-ip:8761 # RabbitMQ UI: http://your-ip:15672 (guest/guest) # Frontend: https://medibook-client-beryl.vercel.app # Backend API: https://medibook-microservices.duckdns.org # Useful Docker commands docker compose logs -f # all logs streaming docker compose restart # restart all services docker compose down && docker compose up -d # full restart docker stats # memory/CPU usage docker compose ps # container status
